classification.difficultyReason: Use Pythagoras’ theorem to establish matching side lengths before deciding congruence.

content.prompt:
Two adjoining triangular areas of land have the dimensions shown.
Use Pythagoras’ theorem to help decide if the two areas of land are congruent.

spec.description: Separate right triangles in opposing orientations, with all dimensions attached to their source sides. Ordinary source blue strokes become house black.
spec.mathematics: The left triangle has perpendicular sides 5 km and 12 km. The right triangle has hypotenuse 13 km and one perpendicular side 5 km. The remaining sides are unlabelled.
spec.answerVisibility: Only supplied dimensions and right-angle marks are visible; calculated lengths remain in answers.

answer.worked:
For the left triangle:
$$\begin{aligned}h^2&=5^2+12^2\\h^2&=169\\h&=13\text{ km}\end{aligned}$$
For the right triangle:
$$\begin{aligned}x^2&=13^2-5^2\\x^2&=144\\x&=12\text{ km}\end{aligned}$$
Both triangles are right-angled, with equal hypotenuses of $13\text{ km}$ and a matching side of $5\text{ km}$. They are congruent by RHS.
